findings.message: DoR check 7 counts English `Scenario:` lines, but this repo's stories are written in pt-BR with `Cenario:`, so every story x-story-create produces fails check 7 and gets NOT_READY. Check 7 says: "Count `Scenario:` lines in story acceptance criteria | `scenario_count >= 4`". `_TEMPLATE-STORY.md:131-144` uses `Cenario:`, and x-story-create/SKILL.md:269 says "Write Gherkin scenarios in Portuguese (DADO/QUANDO/ENTAO/E/MAS)". This story (plans/epic-0028/story-0028-0002.md) has 6 `Cenario:` lines and no `Scenario:` lines. So `/x-story-plan story-0028-0002` counts 0 and returns NOT_READY even though the story has 6 scenarios.

The skill forces English output, the opposite of RULE-006, which the story lists as applicable and which requires all planning-skill output to be in pt-BR. SKILL.md:11 says "**Language**: English ONLY." The story's section 2 lists RULE-006. epic-0028.md defines RULE-006 as "Todo conteúdo gerado por skills de planejamento DEVE estar em português brasileiro (pt-BR)". The sibling planning skills x-story-create/SKILL.md:11 and x-story-epic-full/SKILL.md:11 both say "Portuguese (pt-BR) for all content". All inline artifact formats in Phase 4 and 5 are English.

The reuse check does not match acceptance scenario 2: it compares against the tasks file instead of the planning report and logs a different message, so the required log line "Reusing existing planning artifacts" never appears. The AC says: "DADO que o arquivo planning-report-story-0028-0001.md existe E mtime(story) <= mtime(planning-report...) ... E o log contém \"Reusing existing planning artifacts\"". SKILL.md:93 checks "if the tasks file exists at plans/epic-XXXX/plans/tasks-story-XXXX-YYYY.md", and line 101 logs `"Reusing existing story plan from {date}"`.

Each run edits the story file after writing the tasks file, so on the next run the story is always newer and the plan is always regenerated. That defeats RULE-002 and reruns all 5 subagents every time. Phase 0.3 reuses only when `mtime(story file) <= mtime(tasks file)` (line 101). Phase 4.1 writes tasks-story-XXXX-YYYY.md (line 518), then Phase 4.5 (line 688) says "Read the story file and update Section 8". After any successful run, mtime(story) > mtime(tasks), so the second invocation always takes the "Regenerating stale story plan" branch and the reuse path can never run.

The skill never saves the architecture, test, security or implementation plans the story requires, so DoR checks 1, 2, 3 and 9 ("File exists ...") have nothing to check, especially on the reuse path where no subagent runs. Story section 3.1 says the Architect "Gera architecture plan + implementation plan", QA "Gera test plan", and Security "Gera security assessment". AC scenario 6 refers to tests-story-XXXX-YYYY.md "não foi gerado". Phase 4 (4.1-4.5) writes only tasks, task-plan, planning-report, dor and the story update. Check 1 requires "File exists with layer analysis" and check 9 "File exists with component list". Phase 0.3 reuse says "skip directly to Phase 5 ... Do NOT invoke any subagent", so there is no agent output either.

On READY the story status is never changed to "Pronta para Desenvolvimento", Section 4 DoR checkmarks are never updated, and the DoR result lacks the contract's failed_checks and story_status_update fields. AC scenario 5: "E o status da story é atualizado para \"Pronta para Desenvolvimento\"". Story section 3.3: "Section 4 com DoR checkmarks". Data contract 5.3 requires `failed_checks` and `story_status_update`. Phase 5 only writes the DoR file (line 753) and "Update the planning report's DoR Status section with the verdict" (line 795). Nothing touches the story's Status line or Section 4, and the inline DoR format has only Mandatory/Conditional/Summary/Blockers.

A merged task's Agent field is `merged({agent1},{agent2})`, not the value "MERGED" that acceptance scenario 4 requires. AC: "ENTÃO a task consolidada tem DoD [\"imutável\", \"Bean Validation\"] E o campo Agent é \"MERGED\"". SKILL.md:443: "Source becomes `merged({agent1},{agent2})`". planning-guide.md:82 repeats "Set source to `merged({agent1},{agent2})`".

Adding the core skill directory without regenerating golden files makes the existing GoldenFileTest fail for every profile, so `mvn test` is red at this head. selectCoreSkills() lists every directory under targets/claude/skills/core, so x-story-plan is copied to .claude/skills. CodexSkillsAssembler.assemble then copies .claude/skills into .agents/skills and .codex/skills. GoldenFileTest.validateCompleteness (line 173) fails on any "Extra files (generated, not in golden)". golden/java-quarkus/.agents/skills has x-story-create/epic/epic-full/map but no x-story-plan, and a glob for golden/*/.agents/skills/x-story-plan/** finds nothing.

The change adds no automated test, although the story's DoD requires at least one test checking the SKILL.md frontmatter and required sections. Story DoD: "Pelo menos 1 teste automatizado validando o SKILL.md (sintaxe YAML frontmatter, seções obrigatórias)". Sub-tasks also list a frontmatter unit test, a 6-phase integration test and a golden byte-for-byte match. diff.patch has only three new files (README.md, SKILL.md, references/planning-guide.md) and nothing under java/src/test.

The skill reads the implementation map from `IMPLEMENTATION-MAP.md`, but x-story-map (which the README names as its source) writes `implementation-map-XXXX.md`, so dependency context is always dropped with a warning. SKILL.md:81: "Implementation map | `plans/epic-XXXX/IMPLEMENTATION-MAP.md`". x-story-map/SKILL.md:170: "Save as `implementation-map-XXXX.md`". x-story-epic-full/SKILL.md:217 writes the same name. This epic's map is plans/epic-0028/implementation-map-0028.md. So Phase 1.3 always logs "WARNING: Implementation map not found".

The DoR score formula leaves failed mandatory checks out of the total, so a NOT_READY report shows something like "Passed: 7/7" and the checks_total value is wrong. `total_checks = mandatory_passed + conditional_applicable` and `total_passed = mandatory_passed + conditional_passed`. Example: 3 mandatory checks fail and no conditionals apply. Then total_checks = 7 and total_passed = 7, and the DoR file prints "Passed: 7/7" next to "Verdict: NOT_READY". The denominator should be 10 + conditional_applicable.

The staleness check runs before the check that the story file exists, so a missing story with a leftover tasks file can be treated as fresh. The skill then jumps to Phase 5 instead of aborting with "Story file not found" (AC scenario 1). Section 0.3 (line 89) compares `mtime(story file)` with `mtime(tasks file)` and on reuse says "skip directly to Phase 5". Section 0.4 "Verify Story File Exists" (line 106) comes after it and is never reached on the reuse branch. Nothing defines the result when the story file is missing.

MERGE matches only on component and layer and ignores tdd_phase and type, so an Architect GREEN task and a QA RED task (or a Tech Lead VERIFY gate) on the same component collapse into one task. That loses the RED-before-GREEN order and the separate quality gate. Rule 1: "When two or more tasks from different agents target the same component AND the same layer: Merge into a single task". MERGE runs first. Architect tasks get `tdd_phase` GREEN (line 248), and QA RED tasks name the same components (planning-guide example QA-001 `components: [UserValidator, UserValidatorTest]`, layer domain). Rule 2 also says the SEC task must not be removed, yet MERGE has already removed it.

PAIR only creates RED tasks for QA GREEN tasks, so Architect and Security GREEN implementation tasks can have no failing test before them. The planning guide says every GREEN task must have one. SKILL.md:459: "For every QA-NNN GREEN task ... If a GREEN task has no RED counterpart, create a synthetic RED task". The Architect prompt: "Set `tdd_phase` to `GREEN` for implementation tasks" (line 248). planning-guide.md:117: "Every GREEN task MUST have exactly one RED predecessor." Nothing pairs ARCH-NNN or SEC-NNN GREEN tasks.

Story, epic and existing-plan text is pasted directly into prompts for general-purpose subagents with full tools, with no marker treating it as data. A planted instruction in a story could make a planner run Bash or write files, though the planners only need to read. Each subagent block says "Launch `general-purpose` subagent" (e.g. line 209) and inlines `{STORY_CONTENT}`, `{EPIC_CONTEXT_IF_AVAILABLE}` and `{EXISTING_*_IF_AVAILABLE}` directly (line 220 onward). Nothing tells the subagent to treat that text as data or limits it to Read/Grep/Glob. The returned proposals are then written to the story file and to task plans that x-dev-implement later executes (story-0028-0004/0005).

The PO subagent's new Gherkin scenarios are written into the story's acceptance criteria with no human approval, and DoR check 7 then counts them, so the agent can satisfy its own readiness gate. Rule 5 (line 478): "PO amendments are applied to the story's acceptance criteria section". The PO prompt says "Add missing Gherkin scenarios". planning-guide.md:146: "If PO proposes new Gherkin scenarios, they are included in the story file update". Check 7 passes on `scenario_count >= 4` counted in that same section. There is no approval step, and Phase 4.5 only describes Section 8, so where amendments go is also unclear.

Phase 4.5 adds a new Section 8.1 instead of replacing the existing one, so template-based stories (which already have an 8.1 heading) and every regenerated plan get duplicate 8.1 tables. The columns also differ from the template. Line 703: "If Section 8 already exists with sub-tasks, preserve existing content and add Section 8.1 below it." `_TEMPLATE-STORY.md:184-191` already has "### 8.1 Detailed Tasks (Multi-Agent Planning)" with columns `Task ID | Description | Agent | Type | Layer | DoD | Status`. The skill writes `# | Task ID | Description | Type | TDD Phase | Layer | Depends On | Effort`, with no Agent, DoD or Status, and gives no rule for replacing an earlier generated 8.1.

When a regeneration produces fewer tasks, the extra task-plan files from the earlier run are left behind. Downstream PRE_PLANNED execution, which globs `task-plan-TASK-*`, may pick up those orphan tasks. Line 570 writes "One file per task at plans/epic-XXXX/plans/task-plan-TASK-NNN-story-XXXX-YYYY.md". No step deletes earlier task-plan files on `--force` or stale regeneration. story-0028-0004.md:81 consumes `task-plan-TASK-*-story-XXXX-YYYY.md`.

The TASK_PROPOSAL format does not follow the story's data contract (enums, effort format, which fields are required), so consumers built to the contract will see different values. Contract 5.2: source enum ARCHITECT/QA/SECURITY/TECH_LEAD/PO; type DEV/TEST/SEC/QUALITY/VALIDATION; estimated_effort format "Nh"; description ≤ 200 chars; layer, components, tdd_phase and tpp_level optional. SKILL.md:192-203 and planning-guide.md:17-27 use source {AGENT_NAME} ("QA Engineer"), type architecture|test|security|quality-gate|validation, effort XS|S|M|L|XL, no length limit, and make every field except dependencies mandatory.

The skill rejects a story file path as its argument, although the frontmatter contract says the argument may be a STORY-PATH or a story ID. Contract 5.1: argument-hint `"[STORY-PATH or story-XXXX-YYYY]"`. SKILL.md:6 has `argument-hint: "[STORY-ID] [--force] [--skip-dor]"`, and line 71 says "If the argument does not match `story-XXXX-YYYY` format, abort with format error."

The skill gives two different TPP orders, so the QA test-plan order and the consolidated task order disagree, and DoR check 2's "TPP level ordering (1 through 6)" can mean either. QA prompt (lines 282-284): "TPP Level 4 (conditional) ... Level 5 (collection) ... Level 6 (iteration)". Consolidation 3.3 step 3 (line 494) and planning-guide.md:197 order "nil -> constant -> scalar -> collection -> conditional -> iteration".

Final ordering puts every RED task before every GREEN task, so the task list writes all tests before any implementation instead of alternating RED and GREEN per scenario. 3.3: "Order tasks by execution phase: RED test tasks first (TPP Level 1 through 6), GREEN implementation tasks ..., REFACTOR tasks ...". planning-guide.md:195 says "Phase ordering: RED > GREEN > REFACTOR > VERIFY > N/A". This conflicts with the epic's DoD "Tests are incremental".

An anti-pattern line is worded as the opposite of the rule it means to state. Line 848: "Do NOT reorder RED before GREEN pairs (test-first is mandatory)". Read literally, this forbids putting RED before GREEN, which is exactly what Rule 3 requires.

The inline tasks-breakdown template nests a ```mermaid fence inside a ```markdown fence, so the inner closing fence ends the outer block early and the template after it renders or reads wrongly. Phase 4.1 opens ```markdown at line 524, then has ```mermaid at line 549 and ``` at line 552 inside it. The Tasks Table and Escalation Notes that follow are therefore outside the code block.

The DoR verdict that downstream skills use to block or allow implementation is decided by the model on vague criteria ("File exists with layer analysis", "all sections populated"), and the file layout depends on whether the template exists. Phase 5 checks use judgement-based pass criteria. The inline DoR format (Mandatory Checks / Conditional Checks / Summary) differs from `_TEMPLATE-DOR-CHECKLIST.md` (Architecture Readiness ... Final Verdict `{{FINAL_VERDICT}}`), despite line 840 saying "The inline format produces the same conceptual sections". story-0028-0006 reads this verdict to decide BLOCKED.
